work.title: Douce dame jolie / L’espoir que j’ai
work.movement: Complete paired Victor side: Machaut and Janequin in later arrangements

version.value: Two songs from J.-B. Weckerlin’s Échos du temps passé, volume I, performed with harp and lute
version.note: The label numbers Machaut’s Douce dame jolie first and Janequin’s L’espoir que j’ai second; DAHR quotes the collection title and volume from Victor’s ledgers. BnF describes the published collection as voice with piano, so the precise harp-and-lute adaptation is not established from that score.

date.value: Fourteenth- and sixteenth-century songs; nineteenth-century published arrangement collection
date.note: The label prints 1350 A.D. and 1530 A.D. as historical song dates; these are retained only as label assertions, not verified composition dates. BnF dates volume I to 1853–1857.

completeness.value: Entire published two-song acoustic side; not a complete original Machaut virelai
completeness.note: No digital mid-phrase extract is made. Original stanza completeness and the exact boundary between the two arranged songs are unestablished; the side remains one authored section.

performers.note: DAHR identifies Raymond Dixon as Murphy’s pseudonym, not a second singer. Di Stefano is credited for takes 3–4; Francis J. Lapitino belongs only to discarded takes 1–2 and is not credited on this issued take.

date.note: Take 4 was made on 17 March 1915. The earlier matrix date 14 January 1915 refers to destroyed takes 1–2, not the recording streamed here.

place.value: New York, New York, United States
place.note: DAHR specifies New York for takes 3–4. Camden belongs to the January takes and is not substituted for this session; the studio address is unknown.

label.value: Victor Talking Machine Company; blue label
label.note: The viewed label names Victor and Lambert Murphy and specifies tenor with harp and lute, in French.

catalogue.note: The side suffix B is visible on the label. LOC and DAHR identify the 10-inch carrier.

matrixTakeSides.note: DAHR marks take 4 as Master and links the same audio. Matrix/take identification comes from discographic records, not from claiming to read an illegible run-out inscription.

publication.note: Bolig’s entry 45083 gives May-16 as release date. This corrects the Archive mirror’s claim of first publication in 1915, which conflates release with the session year.

credits.value: Source disc: UCSB Davidson Library, Department of Special Collections; National Jukebox digital access; Hessel Digital Library mirror
credits.note: LOC identifies the source collection. The mirror credits digitisation to the Library of Congress Packard Campus; DAHR also describes the audio as from the UCSB Library. No individual transfer engineer is established.

date.note: The original disc-transfer date is unknown. The Archive mirror states LOC retrieval on 30 September 2026 and repository publication on 10 October 2026; neither is the 1915 session or 1916 release.

processing.value: Archive describes its MP3 as a bit-exact copy of the LOC-served MP3, with no processing
processing.note: This records the mirror’s provenance statement, not an independently performed checksum comparison. Original stylus, speed correction, equalisation and noise-reduction settings are unknown. No additional audio cut is made.

digital.format: MP3 mirror of the complete National Jukebox side

composition.value: Historical songs and Weckerlin collection are outside ordinary composition copyright terms
composition.note: BnF gives Weckerlin’s dates 1821–1910 and the collection’s publication in 1853–1857. The exact person responsible for adapting its piano accompaniment to harp and lute is not established. Recording admission rests independently on the documented pre-cutoff publication.

recording.value: Rule 2 — United States public domain: published May 1916
recording.note: Victor 45083’s documented 1916 publication precedes the project’s 1925 cutoff. source.rights uses us-published-before-cutoff with published 1916. The Archive Public Domain Mark is corroborative, not the sole basis; its 1915 first-publication claim and simplified statutory explanation are not repeated. This is a US basis, not a claim of worldwide clearance.

rights.creditLine: Machaut, Douce dame jolie, and Janequin, L’espoir que j’ai, from Weckerlin’s Échos du temps passé; Lambert Murphy, tenor, Stefano Di Stefano, harp, William Carlino, lute. Recorded New York, 17 March 1915; Victor 45083-B, matrix B-15595, take 4; released May 1916. Source disc UCSB; Library of Congress, National Jukebox; Hessel Digital Library mirror on Internet Archive. US public-domain recording.

editorial.timing: audio.mjs analyze completed before annotation; cache/analysis/origins-machaut-douce-dame-jolie.txt was read. Its novelty peaks do not establish which song is sounding. The complete paired side is one section, with no invented inter-song transition or cut point. Three cues use the short-recording exception.
editorial.orchestra: Omitted with reason: the documented accompaniment is harp and lute, whereas the identified Weckerlin publication is for voice and piano. No score of the exact recorded adaptation was verified; a piano score is not used to invent the distribution of harp and lute notes.
